demo-offline-suport.webm

Set up the Panorra PWA project foundation so the team has a stable starting point for development. This task should cover the initial app setup, core configuration, and the basic structure needed for future PWA work.

RESULT

PWA foundation audited end-to-end and confirmed in place, verified against a real production build (dist/panorra-pwa/browser/ngsw.json), not just source inspection.

Manifest (src/manifest.webmanifest) — id/scope/start_url consistent, theme_color synced with index.html, 192/512 icons present. Deferred (documented, not a bug): maskable icon variant and screenshots — both need new design assets.

Service worker registration (app.config.ts:40-43) — provideServiceWorker('ngsw-worker.js', { enabled: !isDevMode(), registrationStrategy: 'registerWhenStable:30000' }). Previously two service workers (ngsw-worker.js + a hand-rolled src/worker.js/src/client.js) registered at the same scope and fought each other; that pair has been removed entirely and push notifications moved onto SwPush (push-notification.service.ts).

Cache strategy (ngsw-config.json), verified from the build output:

  • app (prefetch): 111 JS/CSS files, 1.1MB gzip
  • app-icons (prefetch): 7 files — required for splash screen
  • fonts (prefetch): 4 woff2 files
  • lazy-assets (lazy): 179 files — 46MB assets/ + 7.6MB media/, correctly excluded from prefetch
  • navigationRequestStrategy: "freshness" — correct given SSR: online users get live SSR HTML, cached index.csr.html is only the offline fallback
  • No dataGroups — API responses are deliberately never cached

Offline support — layered: NetworkConnectionService (SSR-safe browser online/offline events) → ConnectivityService (real backend reachability probe, not just navigator.onLine, with checking/online/offline state + auto-recovery) → OfflineScreenComponent (full-screen fallback UI with retry/go-home/analytics).

Update mechanism (pwa-update.service.ts) — VERSION_READY prompts a reload toast, unrecoverable forces reload; both guarded on swUpdate.isEnabled, no-op in dev/SSR.

Push notification foundation — frontend complete on SwPush (syncSubscription() never auto-prompts, enablePush() ready for a future settings toggle); backend payload contract change still pending.

Versioning / HTTP cache layer (server.ts:82-114) — hashed bundles get immutable 1-year cache, ngsw.json/ngsw-worker.js get no-cache (prevents clients getting stuck on a stale version), unhashed static assets get a 1-day cache.

Open items (non-blocking):

  1. index.html:27 references apple-touch-icon.png — the correct PNG already exists in the build but isn't linked, so iOS "Add to Home Screen" gets a broken icon.
  2. A couple of leftover debug console.log calls in app.component.ts / connectivity.service.ts need cleanup before merge.
  3. Maskable icon and manifest screenshots still need design assets.

Conclusion: the PWA foundation (manifest, SW registration, caching strategy, offline handling, update flow, push notification skeleton) is complete and solid — sufficient as the team's starting point per this issue's scope.

Demo Offline support

demo-offline-suport.webm

Background

This issue tracks migrating pages from CSR to Angular SSR for SEO. The recurring bug across this whole effort has been one pattern at different layers of the codebase: a component (or the service/facade underneath it) gates its initial data fetch behind isPlatformBrowser(platformId) or an afterNextRender() callback. Neither of those ever executes during server-side rendering, so the page ships an empty shell to crawlers and social-share scrapers — real content only appears after client-side hydration, invisible to anything that doesn't execute JavaScript.

Phase 1 — original checklist items (already closed)

  • Home page — layout/sidebar/header/map SSR'd correctly, but the nearest-places list was gated in HomeFacade.fetchNearestPlaces() (home.facade.ts:229) behind isPlatformBrowser.
  • Detail post — already correct: fetch ungated in ngOnInit, applySeo() runs server-side, JSON-LD included.
  • List place (new panorra) — same root cause as Home page.
  • Detail place (new panorra) — already correct, same pattern as Detail post.

Fixed in commit 7fd5cd4e, which also fixed a second-order issue it exposed: FatchApiService always sent an empty Authorization header server-side because the token was read from document.cookie (doesn't exist server-side). Added getCookieFromHeader() (get-cookie.ts) + AppComponent now injects REQUEST to read the real Cookie header from the incoming SSR request.

Phase 2 — full-app audit (this session, 3 new commits)

Commit 2bf81518 — fix(ssr): remove isBrowser guards blocking initial data fetch in search/explore/hashtag

  • search/{posts,bookmark,users,hashtag} (4 tabs) and explore/{post,bookmark,user,hashtag} (4 tiles) all gated ngOnInit/constructor with if (!this.isBrowser) return; before list.reload().
  • detail-hashtag.component.ts — header and posts fetch effects both gated.
  • Fix: removed the guard from the initial fetch. Scroll-bind effects (genuinely DOM-only) kept their guard.

Commit 965e68a9 — fix(ssr): fetch bookmark/potd content server-side, add missing SEO tags, fix two settings crashes

  • detail-bookmark.component.ts and potd-detail.component.ts had the identical fetch-gating bug, missed by the first pass.
  • Missing SEO: detail-bookmark, detail-hashtag, potd-detail, collection-detail never called SeoService.update() — crawlers/scrapers only saw generic static per-route defaults instead of the real item's title/description/image. Added applySeo() to all four.
  • Two genuine SSR crash risks (actual thrown errors, not just empty content):
    • settings/bookmark.component.ts — ngAfterViewInit() (which does run during SSR) unconditionally attached a real window scroll listener. Fixed with the existing isBrowser guard.
    • settings/bookmark-detail/bookmark-detail.component.ts — a signal field initializer read screen.width directly, throwing ReferenceError server-side. Fixed with a safe default + correction inside afterNextRender() (client-only).

Commit dcfa7245 — fix(ssr): remove facade-level isPlatformBrowser guards blocking SSR fetches (newly discovered, high severity)

  • Re-verifying more broadly (rather than trusting the component-level fixes at face value) surfaced the exact same guard one layer deeper, in the facades underneath the already-fixed components — silently neutralizing those fixes:
    • search.facade.ts — searchPosts/searchBookmarks/searchUsers/searchHashtags/fetchSearchHistories/fetchPostViewCount all returned empty/0 immediately server-side.
    • explore.facade.ts — fetchFeaturedPost/fetchFeaturedUser/fetchHashtagGroup/fetchFeaturedBookmark all returned null.
    • detail-bookmark.facade.ts — getPublishedFolder/getPublishedFolderPosts/getPublishedFolderContributors same.
    • Practical effect: curling /search, /explore, or /bookmark/:slug still returned an empty page even after the component fix, because the facade call never reached the network.
  • potd/potd.component.ts — the list page's potdService.reload() was wrapped inside afterNextRender(), which never fires during SSR, so /potd shipped empty regardless of a redundant isPlatformBrowser check inside that same callback. Moved reload() to fire unconditionally in the constructor; the online/offline listener setup stayed in afterNextRender() (genuinely browser-only).

Verification (applied consistently across all three commits)

  1. npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json — clean.
  2. npx eslint <changed files> — clean (two pre-existing unused-import warnings in search.facade.ts confirmed unrelated to this diff).
  3. npm run build — full production build (browser + server bundles) succeeds.
  4. Served dist/panorra-pwa/server/server.mjs locally and curled the affected routes (/search, /explore, /potd, /bookmark/:slug, /potd/:slug, /collection/:slug, /settings/bookmark, /settings/bookmark-detail/:slug, /hashtag) — all HTTP 200.
  5. Checked the server process's stdout/stderr for crash markers (ReferenceError, window is not defined, screen is not defined) — none found.
  6. After the facade fix, the server log started showing real outbound HTTP calls to views.panorra.com during SSR (401 Unauthorized, expected — the local test has no auth cookie, handled gracefully). Before the facade fix there would have been zero network calls at all, since the facade short-circuited before reaching FatchApiService. This was the concrete proof the fix restored real server-side fetching rather than just looking the same (an empty state looks identical whether it's "no data returned" or "fetch never happened").
  7. Checked raw HTML for og:title tags on each route to confirm SeoService's static-fallback mechanism still works when the dynamic fetch doesn't resolve (e.g. 401/not-found).

Current state

All three commits (2bf81518, 965e68a9, dcfa7245) are already on origin/dev.

Known open items (intentionally not fixed yet)

  • create/create.component.ts — ngOnInit() is fully gated behind isBrowser, skipping category/address-token fetch and the edit-post-load flow during SSR. Left untouched: authenticated, non-indexed create/edit-post flow with no SEO value, and functionally correct for real users anyway since hydration re-runs the full lifecycle client-side.
  • Auth-cookie coverage — the REQUEST-based cookie read added in 7fd5cd4e fixed the home/places SSR auth path, but I haven't cross-checked whether the routes fixed in this session that need a viewer-token for personalized content (search, explore, bookmark detail, potd) are fully covered by that same mechanism, versus just correctly reaching the network and getting an expected 401 for anonymous requests.
